solutionSql:
WITH invoice_rows AS (
  SELECT s.customer_id, i.id, i.amount, i.issued_at
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN shipments s ON s.id = i.shipment_id
),
latest AS (
  SELECT customer_id, id, amount
  FROM (
    SELECT invoice_rows.*,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY issued_at DESC, id DESC) AS rn
    FROM invoice_rows
  ) ranked
  WHERE rn = 1
),
averages AS (
  SELECT customer_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount
  FROM invoice_rows
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT l.customer_id, l.id, l.amount
FROM latest l
JOIN averages a ON a.customer_id = l.customer_id
WHERE l.amount > a.avg_amount
ORDER BY l.customer_id;

ambiguities.phrase: greater than the average of all the customer’s invoices
ambiguities.readingChosen: The average includes the latest invoice, as the word "all" says.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Average only the other invoices. Both readings return the same two rows on the sample (invoices 202 and 204).

notes: Latest invoice by (issued_at, greater id). ROW_NUMBER and DISTINCT ON formulations agree.
